standard_prerequisites.name: Forking independence, Morley sequences and Morley rank in an omega-stable theory
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a complete type p over a set A, a Morley sequence in p over A is an A-indiscernible sequence of realizations of p every finite initial segment of which is independent over A; RM is Morley rank; over an algebraically closed base in an omega-stable theory every type is stationary and has a unique nonforking extension.
standard_prerequisites.use: The first sentence of the proof passes to a base algebraically closed in T^eq so that p becomes stationary, and the last step identifies Morley-ness with independence of the n-th term from the preceding n-1 terms.

standard_prerequisites.name: Kim independence and Kim's lemma for NSOP1 theories
standard_prerequisites.statement: Kim-independence is the independence notion of NSOP1 theories; Kim's lemma says that if a sequence is Morley over a base set, then a type over an extension of that base does not fork over the base.
standard_prerequisites.use: Used at the end of the proof: were the constructed sequence a Morley sequence over A, Kim's lemma would make B independent from a_0 over A, contradicting that the type of a_0 over B forks over A.

standard_prerequisites.name: Compactness and the strict gap below a limit ordinal
standard_prerequisites.statement: First-order compactness, including the extraction of a single formula from a type-definable family, and the elementary fact that below a limit ordinal lambda every ordinal lambda-prime below lambda has a strictly larger ordinal still below lambda.
standard_prerequisites.use: Used twice: to extract the single formula phi from the set sigma of formulas that fork over A, and to choose the Morley rank lambda-prime-prime strictly between lambda-prime and the limit ordinal lambda.

core_obligations: Reduce the type p over A to a type over a base algebraically closed in T^eq: verify that the formula witnessing that p has definable Morley sequences also witnesses this for the extension p-prime of p to the algebraic closure, that nmdeg(p-prime) = nmdeg(p) = F_Mb(p) = F_Mb(p-prime) and RM(p-prime) = RM(p) is still a limit ordinal, so that p may be assumed stationary (source line 2893, first sentence).

With nmdeg(p) = F_Mb(p) = n and q(y) = (p(x)) to the n-th tensor power, form the set sigma of formulas phi(x,y) such that phi(x,a) forks over A for every realization a of q(y), and conclude from compactness and definability of Morley sequences that a nonconstant A-indiscernible sequence is a Morley sequence exactly when it satisfies the negation of every member of sigma at its n-th term (source line 2893).

Extract from sigma a single phi(x,y) with the two properties used later: phi(x, a_0 ... a_n) forks over A for every realization of q(y), and a nonconstant A-indiscernible sequence fails to be an A-Morley sequence exactly when it satisfies phi(a_n, a_0 ... a_{n-1}) (source line 2893).

Fix b_0 ... b_n realizing q(y), write RM(p) = lambda, and prove lambda-prime = RM(phi(x, b_0 ... b_n) union p(x)) is strictly smaller than lambda: otherwise a completion of that type would have Morley rank equal to RM(p) while containing a formula that forks over A, contradicting nonforking over A (source line 2893).

Since lambda is a limit ordinal choose lambda-prime-prime with lambda-prime < lambda-prime-prime < lambda, take q(x) in S(B) extending p(x) with RM(q(x)) = lambda-prime-prime, and take a Morley sequence in q(x) over B; show it is nonconstant and not a Morley sequence over A, because otherwise Kim's lemma would make B independent from a_0 over A although a_0 realizes a type that forks over A (source line 2893).

Close the contradiction by comparing Morley ranks: RM(a_n / a_0 ... a_{n-1}) is at least RM(a_n / B a_0 ... a_{n-1}) = RM(a_n / B) = lambda-prime-prime, and failure to be a Morley sequence over A puts phi(x, a_0 ... a_{n-1}) into tp(a_n / a_0 ... a_{n-1}), so RM(phi(x, a_0 ... a_n) union p(x)) is at least lambda-prime-prime; but a_0 ... a_{n-1} is A-equivalent to b_0 ... b_{n-1}, so the same rank equals lambda-prime, contradicting lambda-prime < lambda-prime-prime (source line 2893).

proof_roadmap.step: Pass to an algebraically closed base in T^eq so that p is stationary, and set nmdeg(p) = F_Mb(p) = n.
Turn the type-definable family sigma of formulas forking over A into one formula phi by compactness, using definability of Morley sequences.
Show RM(phi(x, b_0 ... b_n) union p(x)) is strictly below RM(p) = lambda and choose lambda-prime-prime in the gap left by the limit ordinal lambda.

Build a Morley sequence in a type q of rank lambda-prime-prime over B, check by Kim's lemma that it is not Morley over A, and derive the rank contradiction lambda-prime-prime not greater than lambda-prime.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the theorem labelled nmdegmbdefinablemorleyproperty at source lines 2887-2890: an omega-stable theory has no type p with RM(p) a limit ordinal, nmdeg(p) = F_Mb(p), and p having definable Morley sequences. The argument turns on a strict Morley-rank gap: a single formula phi has to be extracted by compactness out of the set sigma of formulas that fork over A at every realization of q = (p) to the n-th tensor power, and lambda-prime = RM(phi(x, b_0 ... b_n) union p(x)) has to be shown strictly below lambda = RM(p), after which the limit ordinal lambda supplies lambda-prime-prime with lambda-prime < lambda-prime-prime < lambda and a type q in S(B) of that rank (source line 2893). The contradiction then makes one sequence play two roles at once: a Morley sequence in q over B is not a Morley sequence over A, since Kim's lemma would otherwise make B independent from a_0 over A, yet precisely its failure to be Morley over A makes phi(a_n, a_0 ... a_{n-1}) true and forces RM(phi(x, a_0 ... a_n) union p(x)) to be at least lambda-prime-prime, against the A-equivalence of a_0 ... a_{n-1} and b_0 ... b_{n-1}. The reduction to an algebraically closed base in T^eq, the stationarity of p and the two-sided reading of the single formula phi are compressed into one paragraph and are not a routine unfolding of definitions.
